---
title: "Data Leakage"
description: "The unintended use of information during model development that would not be available at prediction time."
term: "Data Leakage"
letter: "D"
category: "Model Evaluation"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Data leakage happens when a model-development process uses information it
would not legitimately have when making real predictions. This can make
evaluation results look much better than actual performance.

## Technical explanation

Leakage can occur when target information enters features, when preprocessing
is fitted using validation or test data, or when related examples appear
across training and evaluation splits. Leakage may be direct or arise
through time, entities, duplicate records, or data collection procedures.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Leaked evaluation can lead teams to deploy models that fail in practice.
Preventing leakage requires understanding how examples are generated,
what information is available at prediction time, and how observations
should be split.

## How it works

Define the prediction time and permissible information, then design splits
and preprocessing around that boundary. Fit transformations only on
training data and apply them to held-out data. Check for duplicates,
shared entities, future information, and target-derived fields.

## Practical example

If predicting whether a customer will cancel next month, a feature recorded
only after cancellation must not be used. Likewise, records for one
customer may need to stay in a single split to avoid identity leakage.

## Common misconceptions

- High validation performance does not prove that leakage is absent.
- Leakage is not limited to a column that directly contains the target.
- Preprocessing on all data before splitting can leak information even if
  labels are not included.
